nodes.label: swe_set_ephe_path()
nodes.rationale: First function to call before any other Swiss Ephemeris function; sets the directory path of the ephemeris files. swe_set_ephe_path(NULL) performs important initializations even when using the Moshier ephemeris. Argument is a single directory or list separated by ; (Windows) or : (Unix); environment variable SE_EPHE_PATH is used if set; built-in path is \sweph\ephe (Windows) or /users/ephe (Unix). Paths longer than 256 bytes fall back to \SWEPH\EPHE. Asteroids are looked up in subdirectories ast0..ast9.

nodes.label: swe_calc_ut() / swe_calc()
nodes.rationale: Core computation functions (swe_calc_ut introduced in v1.60). Compute positions of planets, asteroids, lunar nodes and apogees: swe_calc_ut(double tjd_ut, int32 ipl, int32 iflag, double* xx, char* serr) takes Universal Time; swe_calc() takes Ephemeris/Terrestrial Time (tjd_et = tjd_ut + swe_deltat(tjd_ut)). xx is an array of 6 doubles (longitude, latitude, distance in AU, speed in longitude, speed in latitude, speed in distance). iflag is a 32-bit bit flag (SEFLG_SPEED, SEFLG_JPLEPH/SWIEPH/MOSEPH, SEFLG_HELCTR, SEFLG_TRUEPOS, SEFLG_EQUATORIAL, SEFLG_XYZ, SEFLG_RADIANS, SEFLG_SIDEREAL, SEFLG_CENTER_BODY, ...). Return value >= 0 on success; < 0 for fatal errors (illegal body number, Julian day beyond ephemeris limits, corrupted file), with the message in serr[256]. The ephemeris actually used is indicated by the return value (test against ephemeris flags), since a requested ephemeris may be substituted if its file is missing.

nodes.label: swe_calc_pctr()
nodes.rationale: Calculates planetocentric positions, i.e. positions as observed from another planet (e.g. Jupiter-centric ephemerides): swe_calc_pctr(double tjd, int32 ipl target, int32 iplctr center, int32 iflag, double* xxret, char* serr). Can calculate any object as observed from any other object, e.g. one asteroid from another asteroid or from a planetary moon.

nodes.label: Body numbers (int ipl) in swephexp.h
nodes.rationale: Fixed body numbers select the body for swe_calc(): SE_ECL_NUT=-1 (obliquity and nutation: x[0]=true obliquity, x[1]=mean obliquity, x[2]=nutation in longitude, x[3]=nutation in obliquity), SE_SUN=0, SE_MOON=1, SE_MERCURY=2 ... SE_PLUTO=9, SE_MEAN_NODE=10, SE_TRUE_NODE=11, SE_MEAN_APOG=12, SE_OSCU_APOG=13, SE_EARTH=14, SE_CHIRON=15, SE_PHOLUS=16, SE_CERES=17, SE_PALLAS=18, SE_JUNO=19, SE_VESTA=20, SE_INTP_APOG=21, SE_INTP_PERG=22, SE_NPLANETS=23; SE_FICT_OFFSET=40 (Cupido=40..Poseidon=47, Isis=48, Nibiru=49, Harrington=50, Neptune/Leverrier=51, Neptune/Adams=52, Pluto/Lowell=53, Pluto/Pickering=54); SE_AST_OFFSET=10000 (minor planets: ipl = SE_AST_OFFSET + MPC catalogue number, names in seasantx.txt/seasnam.txt); SE_PLMOON_OFFSET=9000 (planetary moons: ipl = offset + planet_number*100 + moon_number from JPL Horizons; center of body = moon number 99, e.g. 9599 Jupiter COB). Custom fictitious planets (number >= 40) read their orbital elements from seorbel.txt (max 960 user elements; T-terms allowed; 'geo' suffix for Earth-centered bodies).

nodes.label: Fixed star functions (swe_fixstar, swe_fixstar_ut, swe_fixstar2, swe_fixstar_mag)
nodes.rationale: swe_fixstar()/swe_fixstar_ut() compute a fixed star's position from its name; swe_fixstar2()/swe_fixstar2_ut() also return the star name (useful for iteration over the database); swe_fixstar_mag()/swe_fixstar2_mag() additionally return the magnitude. The _ut variants (from v1.60) take Universal Time directly; the plain variants take Ephemeris Time. Used together with swe_set_ephe_path(); the star database is the ~800-star SIMBAD-based file.

nodes.label: swe_nod_aps() / swe_nod_aps_ut()
nodes.rationale: Computes nodes and apsides in several modes: (1) mean positions for nodes/apsides of Sun, Moon, Earth and planets to Neptune, plus osculating positions for Pluto and asteroids (default); (2) osculating for all planets; (3) for planets/asteroids beyond Jupiter, a barycentric ellipse; (4) same as 3 but for Pluto and asteroids beyond Jupiter (the documentation's recommended best choice). In all modes the second focal point of the ellipse can be computed instead of the aphelion.

nodes.label: swe_get_orbital_elements() and swe_orbit_max_min_true_distance()
nodes.rationale: swe_get_orbital_elements() returns Keplerian elements and orbital data (period, perihelion/aphelion dates) of a planet or asteroid; swe_orbit_max_min_true_distance() computes the maximum and minimum true distances of the body.

nodes.label: Eclipse and occultation functions (8.2-8.11)
nodes.rationale: swe_sol_eclipse_when_loc()/swe_sol_eclipse_when_glob() find the next solar eclipse at a given location or globally; swe_sol_eclipse_how() computes the circumstances (magnitude, duration, contact times) of a solar eclipse; swe_sol_eclipse_where() finds the geographic position where an eclipse is central or maximal. Analogous lunar functions: swe_lun_occult_when_loc/glob, swe_lun_occult_where (lunar occultations of bodies by the Moon) and swe_lun_eclipse_when_loc/when/how. A typical eclipse calculation combines when/where with the how function, iterating until the eclipse of interest is bracketed.

nodes.label: swe_rise_trans() and swe_rise_trans_true_hor()
nodes.rationale: Compute rising, setting, and meridian-transit times of a body (planets, Moon, fixed stars) at a given location, as well as heliacal events. swe_rise_trans_true_hor() uses the true (rather than the standard) horizon. A special subsection compares sunrise as defined in astronomy versus in Hindu astrology (the latter using the true horizon / limb of the disc).

nodes.label: swe_pheno(), swe_azalt(), swe_azalt_rev(), swe_refrac()
nodes.rationale: swe_pheno_ut()/swe_pheno() computes planetary phenomena (phase angle, illuminated fraction, elongation from the Sun, apparent diameter, apparent magnitude). swe_azalt() converts ecliptic/equatorial coordinates to horizontal (azimuth, altitude); swe_azalt_rev() does the reverse; swe_refrac()/swe_refrac_extended() compute atmospheric refraction of altitude. These support the heliacal-event and visibility calculations.

nodes.label: swe_heliacal_ut() and swe_vis_limit_mag()
nodes.rationale: swe_heliacal_ut() iteratively determines heliacal rising/setting (evening first / morning last) of the Moon, planets and stars, returning optimum visibility and the visibility start/end times; it uses swe_vis_limit_mag() (the contrast-threshold function based on Schaefer's criterion and the observer's optical/meteorological parameters) to decide whether the object is visible. Limited to latitudes 60S-60N; it does not yet model 'morning last' plus subsequent second heliacal risings for some planets (e.g. Mars). swe_heliacal_pheno_ut() returns additional heliacal details.

nodes.label: Date/time and Delta T functions (9, 10)
nodes.rationale: swe_julday()/swe_date_conversion()/swe_revjul() convert between calendar date and Julian day; swe_utc_time_zone()/swe_utc_to_jd()/swe_jdet_to_utc()/swe_jdut1_to_utc() handle UTC and leap seconds (seleapsec.txt); swe_time_equ()/swe_lmt_to_lat()/swe_lat_to_lmt() relate mean and true solar time. Delta T: swe_deltat()/swe_deltat_ex() compute TT-UT; swe_set_tid_acc()/swe_get_tid_acc() set/get the tidal acceleration used in the calculation; swe_set_delta_t_userdef() allows a user-defined value. Future updates ship in the file swe_deltat.txt.

nodes.label: Sidereal mode functions (12)
nodes.rationale: swe_set_sid_mode() selects the sidereal mode/ayanamsha (SE_SIDM_FAGAN_BRADLEY, SE_SIDM_LAHIRI, SE_SIDM_KRISHNAMURTI, and the various galactic/suryasiddhanta/aryabhata modes, plus SE_SIDM_ECL_T0 / SE_SIDM_SUDDHA and the Vondrak-based modes); combined with the SEFLG_SIDEREAL flag in swe_calc(). swe_get_ayanamsa()/swe_get_ayanamsa_ut() and the _ex variants (swe_get_ayanamsa_ex(), swe_get_ayanamsa_ex_ut()) return the ayanamsha value for a given time; the _ut forms take Universal Time. These implement the 40+ ayanamshas described in swisseph.doc section 2.8.

nodes.label: House functions (swe_houses, swe_house_pos, swe_gauquelin_sector)
nodes.rationale: swe_house_name() returns the name of a house method; swe_houses() computes the house cusps, Ascendant, MC, ARMC, Vertex and East Point for a chosen method; swe_houses_armc() and swe_houses_ex()/swe_houses_ex2() give extended variants (e.g. tropical vs sidereal, different house-method parameters). swe_house_pos() computes the house position of a body (in which house / position within a house); it can also yield the Gauquelin sector position, as can swe_gauquelin_sector(). Beyond the polar circle Placidus/Koch may fail and the function switches to Porphyry with a warning.

nodes.label: swe_sidtime() and swe_sidtime0()
nodes.rationale: Compute sidereal time (swe_sidtime) or sidereal time at mean sidereal time 0 (swe_sidtime0). From SE 2.00, sidereal time is based on the IAU 2006 precession/nutation model; outside the JPL DE431 range (1850-2050) a Vondrak 2011-based solution with a Simon & alii mean-Moon term is used, with constants added for continuity.

nodes.label: The programming steps to get a planet's position
nodes.rationale: Canonical usage flow: (1) swe_set_ephe_path() to set the ephemeris directory (or NULL); (2) swe_julday() to convert the birth date to a Julian day; (3) swe_calc_ut() (or swe_fixstar_ut() for a star) to compute the position; (4) swe_close() to release files and memory. For versions < 1.60 or when working in Ephemeris Time, first convert UT to ET via swe_deltat() and call swe_calc()/swe_fixstar() instead. The miniature sample program swemini.c and the full example swetest.c demonstrate this.

nodes.label: Flag bits (long iflag) for swe_calc()
nodes.rationale: A 32-bit flag selects the kind of computation. Ephemeris choice: SEFLG_JPLEPH (JPL), SEFLG_SWIEPH (Swiss, default via SEFLG_DEFAULTEPH), SEFLG_MOSEPH (Moshier). SEFLG_SPEED adds speed. SEFLG_HELCTR (heliocentric), SEFLG_TRUEPOS (true rather than apparent/geocentric), SEFLG_EQUATORIAL (RA/Dec instead of ecliptic), SEFLG_XYZ (cartesian x,y,z), SEFLG_RADIANS, SEFLG_SIDEREAL (with swe_set_sid_mode), SEFLG_ICRS (DE406 frame), SEFLG_JPLHORA (approximate JPL Horizons), SEFLG_CENTER_BODY (center of body), SEFLG_BARYCTR, SEFLG_NOABERR, SEFLG_NUTNODE. If no ephemeris flag is set the return value contains SEFLG_SWIEPH; incompatible flags are dropped and the ephemeris actually used is reflected in the return code.

nodes.label: swe_close()
nodes.rationale: Releases all resources (open files and allocated memory) used by the Swiss Ephemeris at the end of computations. After swe_close(), no Swiss Ephemeris functions may be used unless swe_set_ephe_path() is called again and, if required, swe_set_jpl_file().

nodes.label: swe_deltat() / swe_deltat_ex()
nodes.rationale: Computes Delta T (TT minus UT) from a Julian day; swe_deltat_ex() (from v2.02) also returns the source/method. The value converts Universal Time to Ephemeris/Terrestrial Time for swe_calc()/swe_fixstar(); swe_calc_ut()/swe_fixstar_ut() apply it internally. The tidal acceleration used can be set with swe_set_tid_acc() and a user-defined value with swe_set_delta_t_userdef(); future updates ship in the file swe_deltat.txt.

nodes.label: seorbel.txt - user-defined fictitious planet orbital elements
nodes.rationale: Text file in the ephemeris path that lets the user define up to 960 fictitious planets. Each line gives epoch (Julian day), equinox (J1900/B1950/J2000/JDATE), mean anomaly, semi-axis, eccentricity, argument of perihelion, ascending node, inclination, and name. T-terms in (t-epoch)/36525 are allowed for all elements except epoch/equinox (except mean anomaly, which is computed from semi-axis and gravity); a 'geo' suffix marks a body moving about the Earth. Swe_calc() reads it when computing a body with ipl >= SE_FICT_OFFSET; otherwise it uses the built-in Uranian-planet elements.
